# Rocket block generator: role-based weeks, block management and adaptation

Worktree: `/Users/luisdeburnay/dev/rocket/.worktrees/m1-core-loop`. INVESTIGATE mode: I read the code and ran the current planner. Nothing was written to the repo. My scratch validation script is `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-luisdeburnay-dev-routr/0f6602a3-b43a-46c6-b392-056cf6dbcf31/scratchpad/weeks.py`.

## 0. What the current generator actually does (measured, not assumed)

I ran `planWeek` and `describeWeek` over every week in `BLOCK_WEEKS`. The complaint understates the problem.

| Week | Current output (Mon to Sun, km) | What is wrong |
|---|---|---|
| 14 Sep (60) | 7.6 / 7.6 threshold (7x4 min) / 7.6 / 7.6 / 7.6 / 22 long with 5.1 km at marathon pace / rest | Threshold 3 days after a maximal half, on the smallest kind of day. Strides on all four easy days. |
| 21 Sep (80) | 10.6 x5, with threshold Wed / rest Sat / 27 long | Rest the day before the long run, and equal days again. |
| 28 Sep (100) | rest / 13.4 x5 (including Sat, the day before Lincoln) / Lincoln 33 | Flat. A 13.4 km day before a 33 km marathon-pace session. |
| 5 Oct (80) | rest / 12.8 x5 / 10K | Flat. |
| 12 Oct (60) | rest / 10.5 / threshold 10.5 on Wed (3 days after the 10K) / 10.5 / 10.5 / rest / 18 long with 7.9 km at marathon pace | Threshold inside the post-race window. A hard long run 6 days before the marathon. |
| 19 Oct (32) | rest / 11 / 9 / 7 / 5 / marathon | Distances fine. Strides every day, and no marathon-pace touch. |

Root causes in code:
1. `placement.distribute()` divides the leftover km evenly across open days.
2. `chooseRestDates()` prefers the day before a hard session. Pfitzinger puts a recovery run there.
3. `describeWeek()` adds strides to every easy day. Its own config comment says "never the day before quality or a long run", and nothing implements that.
4. Nothing models post-race recovery.

**A second defect found while reading: doubles cannot survive a re-plan.** `store.ts replaceWindow` builds `byDate = new Map(editable.map(row => [row.date, row]))`, so both sessions of a double update the same row. One session is lost, and a stale row lingers. `diffWindows` and `toPlanned` are also keyed by date. The new generator uses doubles, so this must be fixed first (stage 5).

## 0.1 Challenges to the prior design (prior-design-extract.md)

- **Monotony.** The extract itself never cites Foster. The citation lives in its parent file, `docs/research/session-prescription-design.json`. That file's own verification marked "keep monotony < 2.0" as OVERSTATED. Measured on daily km, rocket's flat week scores 1.41 (CONFIRMED). The correct taper weeks I generate below score **2.15 and 2.13**, so a km-based "< 2.0" bound would pass the complaint and reject the right weeks. Monotony is a diagnostic here, never a placement rule.
- **Threshold on Wed 16 Sep, day 4 after the half.** Two confirmed expert practices conflict. Higdon Advanced 2 has hills on day 2 and a tempo on day 4. Daniels prescribes 1 easy day per 3 km raced, so 7 days. I choose Daniels because week 2 is also a +72 % volume step. This is labelled a judgement between two confirmed sources.
- **Week-5 "medium-long as a double (12 + 8)".** Not a medium-long run in any system (CONFIRMED: Pfitzinger doubles only on recovery days). This design never labels a double as a medium-long run.
- **Zero threshold in the 100 km week.** More conservative than every coaching system. Kept, because rocket's ratified rule is that a race spends the quality budget. Labelled as a risk choice, not consensus.
- **"Largest Pfitzinger MP block is 12 mi" (short-block sweep, CORRECTED).** Pfitzinger 18/70 week 13 has 14 mi (22.5 km) at marathon pace. Lincoln's 21.1 km is therefore inside Pfitzinger's maximum dose, but 20 days out rather than 5 weeks.
- **18 km with 7.9 km at marathon pace on Sun 18 Oct.** Heavier than any template. It also breaks rocket's own run-in ceiling as an advisory breach. Replaced below (athlete question Q2).
- **Run frequency was never ratified.** The athlete's recorded maximum is 4 runs a week. Pfitzinger gives 4-5 run days up to 88 km (CONFIRMED). Week 2's `minRunDays: 6` is what forces the flat 60 km week (athlete question Q1).

## 1. Session library (config data: `SESSION_LIBRARY`)

Every entry is data: role id, purpose, dose, zone, recovery cost, placement constraints, progression and phases. Paces stay zone multipliers of `PACE_ANCHOR`, anchored on 278.9 s/km:

| Zone | Pace | Heart rate |
|---|---|---|
| Threshold | 4:29 | work mean 172-177 |
| Marathon pace | 5:03 | 158-168 |
| Easy | 5:46-6:19 | ceiling 150 |
| Recovery | 6:19-6:44 | ceiling 138 |

Cross-check: Pfitzinger's general-aerobic pace, 15-25 % slower than marathon pace, gives 5:48-6:18. That matches the existing easy band.

| Role | Purpose | Dose | Zone | Recovery cost | Placement | Progression | Phases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rest` | absorb | 0 km, swim allowed | none | none | day after the long run or race first, then day after quality | none | all |
| `recovery` | volume without cost | 8 km default, 6-10 km | recovery | under 24 h | day before the long run or race; first run after a race | fixed length, does not scale with volume | all |
| `recovery-double` | volume a single slot cannot hold | 10 km AM + 6 km PM, second run at least 25 min, at least 5 h apart | recovery | under 24 h | only by the overflow ladder; never on the day before a hard session; at most 3 a week | none | build, peak, taper |
| `general-aerobic` | aerobic volume | whatever the remainder gives, up to the slot cap | easy | under 24 h | fills the remaining run days | sized off `medium`: each other general-aerobic day is 2/3 of it | all |
| `medium` | the week's second-biggest stimulus | the largest general-aerobic day, up to the single-slot cap (14 km here) | easy | under 24 h | the general-aerobic day furthest from the hard days | none | build, peak, taper |
| `medium-long` | second endurance run | 17.7-24.1 km continuous, 16-23 % of the week, 52-83 % of the long run | 74-84 % HRmax | 24 h | must fit one slot; never a double | +1-2 km a week | build and peak, when feasible |
| `long` | endurance | from the macro layer; spike at most 110 % of the 30-day longest (advisory) | easy | 48 h; next day is rest | the week's anchor day | taper: 60 % then 40 % of the peak long session | all |
| `long-mp` | marathon specificity | marathon-pace km = long run km x phase fraction; at most 20 % of the week and 110 min (Daniels) | easy, then marathon pace | 48 h | as `long`; never inside a post-race window | fraction by phase | build, peak |
| `threshold` | raise the ceiling | 20-25 min early to 30-35 min later; cruise reps with 60-90 s jog; at most 10 % of the week and at most 6.5 km | threshold | 24-48 h | at least 2 days from other hard sessions; after the post-race window; never the day after a long run or race | by minutes, not km | build (and rebuild once the window clears) |
| `taper-touch` | keep intensity while volume falls | 16 min of threshold (4x4) | threshold | 24-48 h | after the post-race window; 7-10 days out | none | taper, 1 week out |
| `dress-rehearsal` | race-pace feel | 11 km with 3.2 km at marathon pace, goal race minus 4 days | easy + marathon pace | under 24 h | does not spend the quality budget | none | race week |
| `shakeout` | race-eve activation | 20-30 min (5 km here) + 4-6 x 80-100 m | easy | none | goal race minus 1 day | none | race week |
| `race-tuneup` | sharpen and calibrate | warm-up + race + cool-down | race | 1 easy day per 3 km raced | spends the week's quality | none | taper |
| `race-rehearsal` | marathon pace inside the long day | the long session | marathon pace | 48 h + 4-5 easy days | is the week's long session | none | peak |
| `strides` (add-on) | turnover, economy | 6 x 20 s on 2 days a week | strides | none | never the day before quality, a long run or a race; blocked by soreness 3 or more | none | all |
| `hill-sprints` (add-on, off) | neuromuscular | 8-12 s, at least 90 s recovery, 4-5 reps rising by 2 a week to 10 | max | none | after an easy run, once a week | reps, then 8 to 10 s | base only; disabled this block (judgement: novel stimulus on top of heavy legs work) |
| `vo2max` (off) | aerobic power | 5 x 1000 m at 5K pace, 2-4 min jog, at most 8 % of the week | VO2max | at least 48 h | 6-8 weeks out (Pfitzinger) | none | race-prep; disabled by the ratified 1-quality budget |

Recovery cost comes from Stanley 2013 (a review): up to 24 h after easy running, 24-48 h after threshold, at least 48 h after high intensity. Only the recovery run's zone and length are encoded from Pfitzinger, as `under 76 % HRmax` and `4-7 mi`. The config's existing 138 ceiling is stricter and stays.

## 2. Week structure as data (`WEEK_STRUCTURE`, `VARIETY`)

**Anchors, in priority order.** These are the long run or race day L, the previous week's L, races and the goal race.

- **L + 1 is rest.** Pfitzinger rests there in 48 of 48 weeks; Hansons runs easy instead.
- **L − 1 is recovery.** Pfitzinger does this in 22 of 33 weeks. A race eve becomes recovery or shakeout.
- **Quality day Q** is the eligible day with the largest minimum gap to hard days. This is the existing `chooseQualityDate`, now with a post-race window added.
- **Q + 1** is the second rest day, if the week has one. Pfitzinger 18/55 rests Thursday after a Wednesday threshold. It is never a rest day before a hard session.
- **The first run after any race is recovery.**
- **`medium`** is the general-aerobic day with the largest minimum distance to hard days (ties go to the earliest).
- **Everything else is general-aerobic.**

**Run days from volume.** Pfitzinger's tiers (CONFIRMED): up to 88 km, 5 days; 88-113 km, 6 days; above that, 7. `minRunDays` stays a floor; the existing semantics are kept. The mandatory rest day always wins.

**Role shares, as bands rather than even splits:**
- Long run: 32-38 % at 54-60 km, 26-31 % at 85-113 km (CONFIRMED; the share falls with volume).
- Quality day: 17.5 % of the week, band 14-25 % (CORRECTED).
- Recovery: fixed at 8 km.
- Other general-aerobic days: 2/3 of `medium`. That ratio sits between Pfitzinger's general-aerobic to medium-long ratio of 0.83 and Higdon's 0.63.
- All km round to 0.5, with the residual going to `medium`.

**Hard/easy spacing.** Quality needs at least 2 days from any hard session (existing guardrail). Never the day after a long run or race (existing). Never inside a post-race window of `round(raceKm / 3)` easy days (Daniels).

**Quality count by phase.** This is the existing `PRESCRIPTION.qualityPerWeek`. A race spends it (existing `racesCountAsQualitySessions`). New: the dress rehearsal does not.

**Variability requirement.** The flat 7.6 x5 week becomes impossible by construction, not by a monotony score. Monotony cannot tell good weeks from bad (CONFIRMED).
- **V1.** The longest non-long running day is at least **1.5x** the shortest, whenever there are 3 or more non-long run days. The lowest confirmed template that is not Daniels is 1.52-1.55; Pfitzinger runs 2.2-3.0. Rocket's flat week scores 1.00.
- **V2.** The quality day is at least the median non-long day and at least 14 % of the week (the quality day is one of the largest days, CORRECTED). Rocket's 7.6 km threshold day fails this.
- **V3.** L − 1 is at most `recovery.maxKm`.
- **V4.** L + 1 is rest.

V1-V4 become rule id `week-structure`. They are blocking for generator output and advisory for athlete edits. Session-RPE monotony and strain (planned minutes x zone RPE) are shown as a diagnostic only. Daniels' long-run cap (25 % or 150 min) and marathon-pace cap (20 % or 110 min) are advisory per-system flags, because Pfitzinger's low-mileage plans routinely exceed them.

## 3. Generation algorithm (replaces `distribute`)

A pure pipeline in `src/domain/planner/placement.ts`, still called by `planWeek(week, options)`. The signature is unchanged, so `today.ts`, `plan.ts`, `daily-pass.ts` and `negotiate.ts` keep working.

1. **`weekContext`.** Gathers slot openings (`openings`, kept); hard anchors (`hardSessions`, kept: a race carrying the long run is one session, and other races are additional to the target); the previous hard date (`previousWeekHardDate`, kept); day ceilings from `raceRunInCeilingKm`, kept inside `dayCapacityKm`; and post-race windows (new).
2. **`chooseRunDays`.** Tier days, floored by `minRunDays`, capped at 7 − minimum rest days (kept).
3. **`assignRoles`.** Applies the order in section 2. The rest-day order becomes after-hard, then after-quality, then earliest. The old "day before hard" preference is deleted. The legs day is fixed here: the quality day, otherwise the non-race long day, otherwise `medium`. Its run is placed in the morning slot when it fits, so `legsMinHoursAfterRun` can hold.
4. **`sizeRoles`.** Fixed sizes first: long or race (macro layer), quality (share), recovery (8), dress rehearsal and shakeout (library, capped by the run-in). The remainder R goes to general-aerobic days: `medium = R / (1 + 2/3 x (n − 1))`, capped by the day's single slot. If R still does not fit, an **overflow ladder** runs in order:
   1. turn recovery days that are not L − 1 into `recovery-double`, where the day ceiling allows;
   2. raise recovery days to 10 km;
   3. turn non-`medium` general-aerobic days closest to hard days into `recovery-double`;
   4. open a run day, removing rest days in reverse preference (the existing loop);
   5. report the shortfall as debt (existing).
5. **`toSessions`.** Kept; it assigns slots per session. Doubles take the morning slot for the AM run and the evening slot for the PM run.
6. **Validate.** `evaluateGuardrails` (existing) plus `week-structure` and `post-race-recovery`.
7. **`describeWeek`.** Kept, now role-driven: threshold minutes by phase; marathon-pace fraction zeroed inside post-race windows; taper long run at 0.4 x the peak long session one week out; dress rehearsal; shakeout; strides on 2 eligible days. `placeStrength` is kept with the new legs-day rule and a ban on double days.
8. **Readiness.** `today.prescribeWeek` and `daily-pass` keep applying `demoteQualityFrom` after generation (existing, unchanged).

## 4. Progression across the weeks

- **Weekly km** is the ratified 60 / 80 / 100 / 80 / 60 / 32 + marathon. The generator never changes a target; it only distributes it. Taper as a share of peak is 80 / 60 / 32 %, against Pfitzinger 18/70's 79 / 61 / 40 (CORRECTED). Race week is cut harder than Pfitzinger.
- **Long run.** 22 → 27 (8 km at marathon pace) → 33 (Lincoln, 21.1 km at marathon pace) → 16 (10K day) → **13** → marathon. Spike ratios against the 30-day longest: 104 % / 123 % / 122 %, with the marathon at 128 %. The last three are advisory and already ratified. The block reaches 25 km or more (Fokkema) and 32 km or more once (Runna).
- **Marathon pace.** 0 (post-race window) → 8 km (30 % of the long run) → 21.1 km (21.1 % of the week, a named breach of Daniels' 20 %; 106 min, inside his 110) → 0 → 0 → 3.2 km dress rehearsal → race. This is steeper than Pfitzinger's 8 / 10 / 12 / 14 mi ladder, and the design names that.
- **Threshold.** 0 → 24 min (5.35 km, inside Pfitzinger's 20-25 min early dose) → 0 (Lincoln spends it) → 0 (10K spends it) → 16 min taper touch → 0. The taper touch is a judgement between Bosquet (keep intensity) and RunnersConnect (last hard workout 12-13 days out). At 16 min it is a touch, not a hard workout.
- **Medium-long run.** Infeasible this block. The weekday slot cap is 14 km, below Pfitzinger's 17.7 km minimum. Every Saturday that could hold one is the eve of a long run, Lincoln or the 10K. The generator emits `medium`, 12-14 km, and the note "no medium-long run: the largest weekday slot (14 km) is under 17.7 km" (athlete question Q3).
- **Doubles.** Only through the overflow ladder: 2 in week 4 and 1 in week 5, all recovery doubles at 16 km, matching Pfitzinger 18/70 week 11. They are labelled availability-forced.

## 5. Block and multi-block management

**State model.** Season → Block (goal race A, start Monday, status) → Phase (`rebuild | build | peak | taper | race | recovery`) → Week (target km, long run, run days, quality budget, ratification) → Session (role, km, slot, zone structure, status).

- Planned versus actual uses the existing `sessions.fulfilled_by_activity_id` and `activities`.
- Compliance is derived: delivered/planned km per week, and key sessions hit.
- Fitness and fatigue are derived: CTL/ATL/TSB from actual sessions only, a trend display that gates nothing (existing).
- Anchors: measured HR in `ATHLETE` (config) and the race result used for `PACE_ANCHOR`.

**Persisted versus derived:**

| Persisted (Postgres) | Derived at read time |
|---|---|
| `blocks` (new, post-race): id, goal race id, start Monday, status, generator version | paces (`derivePaces`) |
| `weeks` + `block_id`, `ratified_at`, `ratification_note` | CTL/ATL/TSB (`rollingLoad`) |
| `sessions` + `role`, `prescription` jsonb (zones and minutes, never paces), unique (date, slot) | compliance, trailing 30-day longest, post-race windows |
| `races` + `effort` (raced / marathon-pace / easy), `result_time_s`, `result_distance_km`, `stopped_s` | readiness verdict, structure validation, monotony diagnostic |
| `plan_proposals` (new): kind, before/after payload, rationale, rule ids, status pending / accepted / declined / expired | the six-week projection beyond the rolling window |
| Existing history tables stay append-only | none |

**Creating a block from a goal race and date** (`proposeBlock`, `BLOCK_TEMPLATE`):
- Weeks to race = N.
- Taper: 3 weeks at 79 / 61 / 40 % of peak (Pfitzinger 18/70) when N is at least 8. Otherwise 2 weeks with a 41-60 % cut (Bosquet).
- Entry week at no more than about 20 % above the trailing 4-week mean. Pfitzinger's plans assume the runner arrives at first-week volume.
- Deload 15-25 % every 3rd-4th week (Higdon, McMillan).
- Long-run ladder capped at 110 % per step (advisory).
- The output is a **proposal**. Volume is athlete-ratified, and acceptance writes `weeks` rows with ratification text. For this athlete the proposal would have peaked well below 100. He ratified 100 with a reversal gate, and that record stands.

**The next block.** After Sat 24 Oct the generator proposes a recovery block, from Pfitzinger's between-marathon 8-week plan (21 / 32 / 41 mi against a 66 mi peak): R1 about 32 % of peak (32 km), R2 about 48 % (48 km), R3 about 62 % (62 km). R1 starts with at least 3 no-run days (Higdon). Easy running from 48 h does not slow recovery (Martinez-Navarro). There is no quality until R2 ends. Then:
- If a next A race is entered: a new block via `proposeBlock`.
- If not: maintenance at the trailing 4-week mean with 3:1 loading (TrainingPeaks, CORRECTED).

## 6. Adaptation: automatic versus surfaced

**Automatic.** These happen inside the ratified week target and come back as a diff plus rationale:
- A single missed session is skipped, not made up. Stryd resumes unchanged for 0-7 days; Runna lets one miss be skipped or moved within the week.
- An extra run triggers the existing spanner absorption: the next quality session is downgraded and the overshoot is given back from easy days.
- Soreness at 3 or more demotes quality and strides (existing, unchanged).
- The post-race window blocks quality and marathon pace.
- Availability loss re-places the week (existing).
- Overflow into doubles.
- A threshold session whose work-interval mean HR is above 180 slows threshold pace by 5 s/km (existing `thresholdVerdict`).

**Surfaced as `plan_proposals`.** Nothing applies until the athlete accepts:
- **Volume.** A week delivered under 85 % of target proposes holding the next week at the delivered level (the existing reversal condition). A gap of 8-14 missed days proposes repeating the phase; 15-28 days, back to base; 29 or more, restart (Stryd ladder). With a fixed race date, the rebuild targets that date (Runna option).
- **Paces.** A marathon-pace HR trend or a race result proposes re-anchoring. That needs a trend across eligible sessions and user acceptance, and it keeps the structure (Runna Pace Insights).
- **Two readiness channels tripped for 7 days** proposes −25 % volume with quality deleted. This rule comes from prior rocket research and was not re-verified here.
- **Frequency, long-run distance and race roles** always go to the athlete.
- **Over-performance** informs the conversation and never raises a target (existing `trend` trigger).

## 7. Sanity check against real templates

- **Week 4** (0 / 16 double / 12 / 13 / 16 double / 10 / 33) most resembles **Pfitzinger 18/70 week 11**: Monday rest, recovery double, recovery before the long run, long run about 31-33 %.
- **Week 3** resembles **Pfitzinger 18/55 week 11**: quality midweek, rest after quality, recovery Saturday, long Sunday at 33-36 %.
- **Week 2** resembles the **Pfitzinger 12-week up-to-55 week 2** shape: 5 runs, long about 37 %.
- **Week 7** is **Pfitzinger 18/70 week 18**: 11 km with 3.2 km at marathon pace 4 days out, strides, short runs.

Every week hits its ratified km. Spread is 1.56-2.2, against 1.00 for the flat week. No run-in breaches remain.

Named deviations:
- Long run above Daniels' 25 % in weeks 2-4.
- Lincoln 21.1 % marathon pace (Daniels cap 20 %) and 178 min (Daniels long-run cap 150).
- A 14 km day two days before the raced 10K, forced by the ratified 80.
- No medium-long run.

## 8. Questions for Luis (self-contained)

- **Q1. Week of 14 Sep: 5 running days instead of 6?** Config asks for 6. At 60 km with a 22 km long run, 6 days forces five runs of 6-9 km, which is exactly the flat week you rejected. Pfitzinger's plans at this volume use 4-5 days, and your recorded maximum is 4 runs a week. Yes: 0 / 8 / 13 / 9 / 8 / 22 / 0. No: the generator keeps 6 days and flags week-structure rule V1.
- **Q2. Sun 18 Oct: 13 km easy instead of 18 km with about 8 km at marathon pace?** Six days before the marathon, 18 km with a marathon-pace block is heavier than every published taper (Higdon: 40 % of your peak long session, which is 13 km). It also breaks rocket's own 13 km run-in ceiling. The 5 km moves into midweek easy days and the week stays 60. Marathon pace instead comes on Tue 20 Oct as 3.2 km inside an 11 km run.
- **Q3. Could one weekday evening hold about 18 km (1 h 45 easy)?** If yes, weeks of 21 Sep to 5 Oct gain a real medium-long run and lose a double. If no, the plan stays as generated and says so.
- **Q4. Which evening is the swim, and when do you lift?** Legs need at least 6 h after the run. On evening-run days that is impossible, so the generator puts the legs-day run in the morning slot (12 km or less).

| Sat 24 | 42.2 | BATTERSEA PARK MARATHON, in carbons. Not counted in the 32. | none |
| Sun 25 | 0 | Rest. Recovery block R1 begins. | none |

Total 32 + race.

### Block checks

- **Guardrails.** Every rocket guardrail passes. The only advisories are the spikes of 27 Sep (123 %), 4 Oct (122 %) and 24 Oct (128 %), all already ratified. There are no run-in breaches.
- **Doubles.** 3 in the whole block, all recovery doubles of 16 km.
- **Km-monotony per week.** 1.22, 1.51, 1.56, 2.15, 2.13, 1.06; the rejected flat week scores 1.41. This is why monotony is a diagnostic only.

ruleToSource.rule: Build weeks from day roles with separate size rules; never divide leftover km evenly
ruleToSource.source: All parsed plans (Pfitzinger 18/55, 18/70, 12/70; Hansons Advanced; Higdon); Runna fixes the long-run day and gives the long run its own progression

ruleToSource.rule: Day after the long run or race is rest (Hansons exception: easy)
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger schedules: rest on 48 of 48 Mondays

ruleToSource.rule: Day before the long run is a short recovery run (6-10 km)
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger: recovery 22 of 33, tune-up race 8 of 33, general aerobic 3 of 33

ruleToSource.rule: Recovery run 6-10 km, fixed length that does not scale with weekly volume, under 76 % HRmax
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 4-7 mi (Dave Bennett blog; 18/55-70 sheet, 5 mi at every volume)

ruleToSource.rule: Run days from volume: up to 88 km 5, 88-113 km 6, above 113 km 7; minRunDays stays a floor
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 18/55 4-5 days, 55-70 plans 6, 70-85 plans 7

ruleToSource.rule: Quality day 14-25 % of the week including warm-up and cool-down; default 17.5 %
Long-run share falls with volume: about 35 % at 55-60 km, 26-31 % at 85-113 km
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger up-to-55 34-36 %; 55-70 plans 26-31 %; Hansons peak 25 %

ruleToSource.rule: Daniels long-run cap: 25 % of the week or 150 min; flagged per system, advisory
ruleToSource.source: sweatelite (25 %), coachray (150 min)

ruleToSource.rule: Non-long day spread: longest at least 1.5x shortest (3 or more non-long run days)
ruleToSource.source: Confirmed templates: Pfitzinger 2.2-3.0, up-to-55 1.55-2.0, Hansons 1.7, Higdon taper 1.52. The 1.5 bound itself is my judgement from those

ruleToSource.rule: Do not use km monotony as the variety rule; session-RPE monotony is a diagnostic only; no 2.0 cutoff
ruleToSource.source: Foster 1998 (sRPE x duration, individual thresholds); recomputed: flat week 1.41 against Pfitzinger 1.49-1.94

ruleToSource.rule: Medium-long run 17.7-24.1 km, a single continuous run, 16-23 % of the week, 52-83 % of the long run; only where one slot holds it
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 18/55, 18/70 transcriptions; Dave Bennett blog (74-84 % HRmax, 10-20 % slower than marathon pace)

ruleToSource.rule: A double is never a medium-long run, long run or quality session; it splits a recovery day about 60/40
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 18/70: always 6 mi AM + 4 mi PM on recovery days

ruleToSource.rule: Doubles: second run at least 25 min; runs at least 5 h apart; at most 3 a week; never on the day before a hard session
ruleToSource.source: Buena Vida 70-85 review (25 min); RunnersConnect doubles (5 h, 2-3 a week, not before hard)

ruleToSource.rule: Doubles only by the overflow ladder, labelled availability-forced; they are not a performance tool
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger first double at 66 mi; Yeo 2008 (no time-trial difference); Kjosen Talsnes 2024 (lower internal load)

ruleToSource.rule: General-aerobic run: 15-25 % slower than marathon pace, up to 16 km, 70-81 % HRmax
ruleToSource.source: Dave Bennett blog (pace); runningwithrock Pfitzinger explainer (HR)

ruleToSource.rule: Other general-aerobic days are 2/3 of the medium day
ruleToSource.source: Between Pfitzinger's 0.83 (general-aerobic to medium-long) and Higdon's 0.63 (short to midweek runs)

ruleToSource.rule: Threshold at most 10 % of weekly km; rocket's absolute cap 6.5 km stays
ruleToSource.source: Daniels (coachray); rocket PRESCRIPTION

ruleToSource.rule: Threshold progressed by minutes: 20-25 min early, longer later; cruise reps with short jog
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 4th ed (runningwithrock); Haugen 2022 (1 min recoveries)

ruleToSource.rule: Minimum gap between hard sessions: easy up to 24 h, threshold 24-48 h, high intensity 48 h or more
ruleToSource.source: Stanley, Peake & Buchheit 2013

ruleToSource.rule: After a race, 1 easy day per 3 km raced before quality or marathon pace
ruleToSource.source: Daniels' Running Formula (Human Kinetics excerpt)

ruleToSource.rule: Short quality from day 2-4 and a full long run on day 7 after a half (the alternative not chosen)
ruleToSource.source: Higdon Intermediate 2 / Advanced 2, weeks 9-10
ruleToSource.grade: expert-practice (CONFIRMED); choosing Daniels over it = judgement

ruleToSource.rule: First run after a race is recovery; easy running from 48 h is fine
ruleToSource.source: Martinez-Navarro 2021 RCT; Costello 2020 (jump height and soreness back by 48 h)

ruleToSource.rule: No quality for 4-5 days after a big marathon-specific session
ruleToSource.source: Canova lecture (runningwritings); RunnersConnect special block (5-7 days)

ruleToSource.rule: Race spends the week's quality budget; marathon pace inside a long run does not count
ruleToSource.source: rocket ratified guardrail; consistent with Pfitzinger 18/70 week 16 (no other quality that week)
ruleToSource.grade: code owns truth; general rule UNVERIFIABLE in short-block sweep (judgement)

ruleToSource.rule: Marathon pace inside the long run: at most 20 % of the week and 110 min per session; Pfitzinger maximum 14 mi (22.5 km)
ruleToSource.source: Daniels (coachray; sweatelite says 90 min / 16 mi, a disagreement); Pfitzinger 18/70 week 13

ruleToSource.rule: Taper long run at about 60 % of the peak long session 2 weeks out and 40 % 1 week out
ruleToSource.source: Higdon Intermediate 1 weeks 15-17 (20 / 12 / 8 mi)

ruleToSource.rule: No marathon pace in the taper long run (proposal: config fraction 0.44 becomes 0)
ruleToSource.source: RunnersConnect (last hard workout 12-13 days out); Pfitzinger race-week marathon pace limited to 2 mi

ruleToSource.rule: Race-week dress rehearsal: 11 km with 3.2 km at marathon pace, 4 days out; does not spend the quality budget
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 18/70 week 18 (7 mi with 2 mi at marathon pace, Wednesday before a Sunday race)

ruleToSource.rule: Shakeout 20-30 min + 4-6 x 80-100 m, 18-24 h before the race
ruleToSource.source: RunnersConnect

ruleToSource.rule: Taper keeps intensity and frequency; cuts volume 41-60 % over about 2 weeks; 16-min threshold touch
ruleToSource.source: Bosquet 2007 meta-analysis; touch dose is judgement against RunnersConnect's 12-13 days

ruleToSource.rule: Strides on a couple of easy days a week, never the day before quality, a long run or a race
ruleToSource.source: Daniels (Human Kinetics excerpt: strides on a couple of E days); rocket config comment
ruleToSource.grade: expert-practice (CORRECTED; count of 6 x 20 s not in source = existing rocket judgement)

ruleToSource.rule: Single session at most 110 % of the trailing-30-day longest run; advisory, never blocking
ruleToSource.source: Frandsen 2025 BJSM, 5,205 runners

ruleToSource.rule: No ACWR gate; week-to-week ratio is not a gate
ruleToSource.source: Impellizzeri 2020; Lolli 2019; Frandsen 2025 (negative dose-response); Damsted 2019 (day-21 window)

ruleToSource.rule: Peak long run 25 km or more; 32 km or more at least once
ruleToSource.source: Fokkema 2020 (under 25 km adds 13.4 min); Runna long-run article

ruleToSource.rule: Block template taper 79 / 61 / 40 % of peak over 3 weeks
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 18/70 (12/70: 81/63/40; 18/55: 78/58/40); Smyth & Lawlor 2021 strict 3-week taper

ruleToSource.rule: Deload every 3rd-4th week by 15-25 %
ruleToSource.source: Higdon (every 3rd, 55 to 38 mi); McMillan PDF; 80/20

ruleToSource.rule: Entry week about equal to the trailing base; largest step about 20 %
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger 12-week plans (Buena Vida): the runner arrives at first-week volume

ruleToSource.rule: Post-marathon recovery weeks at about 32 / 48 / 62 % of peak, starting with rest days
ruleToSource.source: Pfitzinger between-marathons 8-week plan (21/32/41 mi against 66); Higdon (3 days no running)

ruleToSource.rule: Missed-days ladder: up to 7 resume; 8-14 repeat phase; 15-28 back to base; 29 or more restart. Beyond 7 days it becomes a proposal
ruleToSource.source: Stryd adaptive training FAQ

ruleToSource.rule: Realignment offered (not applied) after more than 3 missed sessions or a missed week; with a fixed race, rebuild to the race date
ruleToSource.source: Runna Plan Realignment

ruleToSource.rule: Pace changes only on a multi-session trend plus athlete acceptance; structure kept; easy runs never repaced
ruleToSource.source: Runna Pace Insights

ruleToSource.rule: Gym load counts as scheduled load; legs on the quality day, else the non-race long day, else the medium day; never on a double day; that day's run in the morning slot
ruleToSource.source: Athlete instruction (legs on hardest day); Garmin DSW failure when gym load is unseen (the5krunner). 'Hardest = quality first' is my reading

ruleToSource.rule: Intensity choice (pyramidal vs polarised) is a risk decision, not a performance optimum
ruleToSource.source: Oliveira 2024 meta-analysis (time-trial SMD -0.01); Festa 2019
